inputs.source: Customer-authored email body received by the support mailbox

instructions.note: 'You may look up any customer by email or account id' lets the agent resolve any account named in an untrusted email, with no check that the requester owns that account.
Cross-customer confidentiality is enforced only by a prompt rule, with no technical check binding the requester's identity to the account read.
'Do not wait for a human unless the customer is angry' leaves the escalation trigger to the model's own judgment, with no structural approval gate, before an irreversible external send.

controls.name: Prompt rule against cross-customer disclosure
controls.decay_rationale: Enforcement depends entirely on the model choosing to follow prompt.md:14; a more capable or adversarially-prompted model can rationalize exceptions or be convinced the lookup is authorized.

controls.name: Escalate to human only if customer appears angry
controls.decay_rationale: The decision to involve a human rests on the model's own judgment of tone, with no structural gate, and is not applied before send in the common case.

controls.name: Outbound email logged to SIEM
controls.decay_rationale: Logging is enforced outside the model and does not depend on model behavior, but it is detective only and occurs after the email has already left, so it does not prevent disclosure.

controls.name: Human approval gate on external send (missing)
Recipient confirmation bound to the originating ticket (missing)
Tool definition pinning/hashing for crm_mcp and mail_mcp (missing)
Mutual or signed identity verification for MCP servers (missing)
Binding requester identity to the account looked up (missing)

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): untrusted email drives CRM lookup and direct external send of confidential data

attack_path.note: Attacker-controlled email body can name any account id or email address
Agent looks up the named account using a broad-privilege CRM token, with no check that the requester owns it (prompt.md:3)
Agent sends the looked-up data directly using a shared mail credential that can reach any address (prompt.md:5-6)

forecast.watch_signal: Model id/version string changes in platform config with no separate review (subject.model.swappable=true).

evidence.observation: Agent reads the customer's email and may look up any customer by email or account id, with no check that the requester owns the account.
Routine answers are sent directly with send; a human is consulted only if the model judges the customer is angry.
The only control against cross-customer disclosure is a prompt instruction, not a technical check.
crm_mcp and mail_mcp are both called with static bearer tokens (CRM_SVC_TOKEN, MAIL_SVC_TOKEN).
CRM_SVC_TOKEN can read every customer record; MAIL_SVC_TOKEN is a shared service account that can send to any address.

recommendations.action: Scope CRM_SVC_TOKEN to per-request least privilege, or add a server-side authorization check that the requested account id or email matches the verified identity of the ticket's sender before returning data.

Add a human approval gate with raw_action review on cap.email_send whenever the drafted response contains data about an account other than the one tied to the verified sender, or whenever the recipient is not the original sender's verified address.

Replace the shared MAIL_SVC_TOKEN with a scoped send capability that can only reply to the verified sender address of the originating ticket, so the destination is bound to the system of record rather than chosen by the model.
Add a pre-send check that flags outbound emails whose recipient or content does not match the originating ticket's verified sender or account, rather than relying only on after-the-fact SIEM review.

findings.title: Agentic Supply Chain Vulnerability (ASI04): unpinned, unverified MCP tool definitions for crm_mcp and mail_mcp

attack_path.note: Static bearer token auth; no peer identity verification; tool definitions not pinned or hashed
Broad-privilege read reachable through the unverified, unpinned server
Static bearer token auth; no peer identity verification; tool definitions not pinned or hashed
Shared-credential, any-address send reachable through the unverified, unpinned server

findings.residual_rationale: ctrl.prompt_no_cross_share and ctrl.escalate_if_angry nominally cover cap.crm_read and cap.email_send, which would mechanically credit step 4 and float residual to high. But both controls operate on the model's own choices; if the tool definition itself is tampered with (a rug pull or poisoned schema on an unverified, unpinned server), data can be altered or exfiltrated below the model's visible decision path, so these prompt-level controls provide no real protection against this specific vector. No other declared control covers it, so residual is held at the inherent tier of critical.

forecast.watch_signal: New entries appear in either server's tools/list response, or a tool's schema/description hash changes, without a corresponding review and re-pin.

evidence.observation: Both crm_mcp and mail_mcp are configured with only a bearer token header; no pinning, hash, or signature fields are present for either server's tool definitions.

CRM_SVC_TOKEN and MAIL_SVC_TOKEN are both broad or shared credentials, so a tampered tool definition on either server could read or send far beyond what a single ticket requires, with no independent check.

recommendations.action: Pin or hash tool and server definitions for crm_mcp and mail_mcp; verify the hash on every connection and alert on any change before the tool is used.
Verify MCP server identity with mTLS or signed certificates instead of relying on a bearer token alone.
Move both services from broad or shared credentials to least-privilege, per-action scoped credentials so a compromised or tampered tool definition cannot read or send beyond a single ticket's needs.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is critical: an untrusted customer email can drive a broad-privilege CRM read followed by an irreversible external send to any address (TC1 lethal trifecta), and both MCP connections lack peer identity verification and tool definition pinning (ASI04 supply chain). The trifecta finding's only present controls are two behavioral prompt instructions plus after-the-fact SIEM logging, which reduce it by one tier to high, but the supply-chain finding has no preventive or containment control at all, so overall residual remains critical. Forecast stays critical: the trifecta finding's behavioral controls are dependent and documented to decay because the model is upgraded with the platform with no separate review, and the supply-chain finding has no control left to decay further.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration in prompt.md, mcp.json, and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.

No full tool manifest (argument schemas) was provided beyond the tool names get_customer and send; capability scope is inferred from the prompt and runtime notes, so some fields carry medium confidence.
peer_identity_verified and definitions_pinned are inferred as false from the absence of any pinning or verification configuration in mcp.json, not from an explicit negative statement.

No server-side authorization logic was provided; it is assumed that identity binding between the emailing customer and the looked-up account is enforced only by the prompt instruction at prompt.md:14, since no other mechanism is described.
